findings.why: The upstream action was unconditional (call the hotline when despairing). The adaptation correctly narrows 116 123 to adults, but gives a reader under 18 no alternative path at all besides 112. The stored snapshots contain a ready fallback (the children and youth line) that the item drops. This is the same pattern as dropping the fallback when the preferred option is not offered, in a crisis context where the reader may be a minor.

findings.fix_direction: State a path for a reader under 18 (or say explicitly that the item is written for adults and point to the children and youth service), using only contacts confirmed in the stored official pages.

findings.why: With the cross-reference links removed, the headline action names no one to contact and no route to get there. The only concrete contacts left are the crisis line and 112. A reader with persistent low mood who is not in crisis, or whose symptoms are severe (Ograniczenia#2 only says they need clinical assessment, with no action), gets no actionable route. The stored Ministry page describes a walk-in route that needs no referral and a 24 hour information line. The sentence is not unsafe, so this stays minor.

The sentence is conditional and low risk, but the action is wider than the one the source measured and the item does not call this an editorial example.

findings.why: The letter A is attached to the whole item, but it describes only the exercise meta-analysis. The headline action (seek support) and the hotline content rest on official information pages, which the README places under operational guidance (C), not on a measured effect. The field does not say which clause the A covers, so the strong A and the conditional movement clause are merged under one letter. The low-certainty caveat is stated, which limits the harm.
